q: Which of the following is the ideal flushing mechanism for water closets considering the user is a PWD?
n: Lever-type flush controls can be worked with a closed fist or an elbow, without tight grasping, pinching or twisting. That makes them the accessible choice for persons with disabilities. Source: BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, Toilets and Baths (operable parts); ADA Standards, Sec. 309.4 / 604.6.

q: Who developed the Greater London Plan of 1944 following World War II?
n: Sir Patrick Abercrombie prepared the County of London Plan (1943) and the Greater London Plan (1944) for post-war reconstruction. They introduced the green belt and the new towns. Source: Hall, Cities of Tomorrow; Gallion & Eisner, The Urban Pattern.

q: It refers to the creation of artificial new land.
n: Land reclamation creates new land from the sea, riverbeds or lake beds by filling or draining them. Source: Philippine Reclamation Authority (EO 525 / EO 74); Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: This type of earthwork involves balancing cut and fill.
n: Land grading reshapes the ground surface to the required levels and slopes. It is designed so that cut volumes balance fill volumes, which minimizes hauling. Source: De Chiara & Koppelman, Time-Saver Standards for Site Planning (Grading and Earthwork).

q: Where is the first Garden City located?
n: Letchworth Garden City (1903), planned by Raymond Unwin and Barry Parker, was the first garden city built on Ebenezer Howard's model. Welwyn followed in 1920. Source: Howard, Garden Cities of To-morrow; Hall, Cities of Tomorrow.

q: A compendium of principles, beliefs, and values that architects are expected to adhere to in the conduct of their personal and professional dealings.
n: The Architect's Credo is the UAP's compendium of the principles, beliefs and values that architects are expected to follow in their personal and professional dealings. Source: UAP Architect's Credo; UAP Code of Ethical Conduct.

q: Who is automatically accredited as a CPD Provider for architects?
n: Under the IRR of RA 9266, the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA) is automatically accredited as a CPD provider. The Board accredits other providers. Source: RA 9266 IRR and RA 10912 (CPD Act of 2016) IRR.

q: It is the database of all registered architects.
n: The Board keeps a roster of all registered architects, with their registration details. It is updated and published regularly. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23 (Roster of Registered and Licensed Architects).

q: Who shall initiate the establishment of reciprocity for foreign citizens who want to take the licensure examination in the Philippines?
n: A foreign applicant must prove that their country admits Filipino architects to its licensure exam on equal terms. So reciprocity is established on the applicant's initiative, with documentary proof submitted to the PRC. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 27 (Reciprocity Requirements).

q: In socialized housing, what can be used to increase density?
n: BP 220 allows pathwalks (minimum 3.0 m wide, up to 60 m long) as the only access to socialized housing lots. Lots can front a pathwalk instead of a road, which raises density. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Design Standards – Circulation (Pathwalks).

q: In professional practice, CPD means what?
n: CPD stands for Continuing Professional Development, the training and education professionals must earn to renew their licenses. Source: RA 10912 (Continuing Professional Development Act of 2016), Sec. 3.

q: When was the Philippine Green Building Code approved by the DPWH?
n: The Philippine Green Building Code, a referral code of the National Building Code, was issued by the DPWH in June 2015. Source: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Referral Code of PD 1096.

q: BP 220 applies to the development of what?
n: BP 220 sets the minimum standards and technical requirements for economic and socialized housing projects. Open-market housing falls under PD 957. Source: BP 220 (1982) and Revised IRR (2008), Sec. 1 (Scope).

q: The architect identifies the site’s potential and development controls considering the surroundings. What service is provided?
n: Site selection and analysis covers finding and evaluating candidate sites. It looks at their potential, the development controls that apply (zoning, setbacks, height limits) and the surroundings. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Pre-Design Services – Site Selection and Analysis.

q: It involves the use of secondary data in the client’s decision-making. The architect can help by providing what service?
n: Pre-feasibility studies rely mostly on secondary data (existing records, published statistics) to screen whether a project is worth a full feasibility study. That helps the client decide early. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Pre-Design Services – Pre-Feasibility and Feasibility Studies.

q: A large controversial project is proposed and the public has mixed reactions to it. How can an architect help?
n: Promotional services prepare presentation materials, models and campaigns to explain a project to the public and stakeholders. That builds acceptance for a controversial development. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Pre-Design Services – Promotional Services.

q: It comes after the project definition phase during a regular design service.
n: In regular design services, the project definition phase is followed by the Schematic Design Phase, then Design Development, Contract Documents, Bidding and Construction. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Detailed Architectural Design Services – Phases.

q: Which of the following is the most famous example of classical superposed order?
n: The Colosseum stacks the orders on its facade: Tuscan/Doric on the ground floor, Ionic on the second and Corinthian on the third, with Corinthian pilasters above. It is the classic example of superposed orders. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Roman); Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which classical order has the shortest columns?
n: The Tuscan order is the simplest and has the stoutest proportions, with a column height of about 7 diameters. The Doric is about 8, Ionic 9, and Corinthian and Composite 10. Source: Vignola, Regola delli cinque ordini; Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture (Orders).

q: Which classical order was used in the portico of the Pantheon?
n: The portico of the Pantheon in Rome has 16 monolithic granite columns with white marble Corinthian capitals. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Roman); MacDonald, The Pantheon.

q: Which classical order was used in the Parthenon?
n: The Parthenon (447–432 BC, Ictinus and Callicrates) is the supreme Doric temple. Ionic elements appear only in its interior and frieze. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Greek); Fazio, Moffett & Wodehouse, A World History of Architecture.

q: Which classical order was used in the Erechtheion?
n: The Erechtheion on the Acropolis is an Ionic temple, famous for its Porch of the Caryatids. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Greek); Fazio, Moffett & Wodehouse, A World History of Architecture.

q: Republic Act No. 11201, the law that established the new Philippine government department responsible for housing and related developments, was signed in what year?
n: RA 11201 created the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD). It was signed on 14 February 2019. Source: RA 11201 (Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development Act).

q: Who introduced “region” in urban planning theory?
n: Patrick Geddes, a Scottish biologist and planner, introduced the region as the basis of planning (the "valley section" and survey-before-plan). He also coined the term "conurbation". Source: Geddes, Cities in Evolution (1915); Hall, Cities of Tomorrow.

q: Who is the Danish urban planner and architect who leads in people-centered urban design, prioritizing pedestrians and cyclists?
n: Jan Gehl is the Danish architect and urban designer known for people-centered design that prioritizes pedestrians, cyclists and public life (Life Between Buildings, Cities for People). Source: Gehl, Cities for People (2010).

q: Who is the Filipino architect who assisted Harry Frost in developing the original plan for a new postcolonial capital city in 1941?
n: In 1941, American planner Harry Frost, with Filipino architect Juan Arellano and engineer Alpheus Williams, drew up the original plan for Quezon City as the new national capital. Source: Quezon City Government history; Hall & Alcazaren, Quezon City planning histories.

q: Your architectural firm works with an international design firm based in London. They invited a representative from your firm to attend their event celebrating World Architecture Day. When is World Architecture Day?
n: World Architecture Day, declared by the International Union of Architects (UIA), falls on the first Monday of October together with World Habitat Day. Source: International Union of Architects (UIA), World Architecture Day.

q: What does DAEDS mean?
o: Detailed Application of Engineering Design and Specifications
Detailed Architectural and Engineering Development Service
Department of Architecture and Engineering Design School
Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Service
n: DAEDS stands for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services. Under it, the architect provides the architectural design together with the allied engineering design under one contract. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 6 (DAEDS).

q: A newly licensed architect becomes what kind of member of the UAP?
n: A newly licensed architect who joins the UAP becomes a regular member. Fellowship and honorary membership are conferred, and charter members are founders. Source: UAP By-Laws (Membership Classes).

q: Which principle of design is the most important in designing for accessibility?
n: Contrast in color, luminance and texture is the key accessibility principle. It helps people with low vision find doors, steps, edges and signs. Source: BP 344 2024 Revised IRR (visual contrast); ISO 21542 (Accessibility of the Built Environment).

q: A principle of design that creates a feeling of organized movement.
n: Rhythm is the regular or patterned repetition of elements, which leads the eye through a composition with a sense of organized movement. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order (Rhythm); Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: It creates a sense of harmony between all parts of a work of art.
n: Unity is the sense that all parts belong together and form a coherent whole. It is the result of harmony and consistency among the elements. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Unity and Variety).

q: Which of the following can best articulate the door element in the room?
o: placing it at the center of the wall
painting it with a light color
n: Articulation makes an element read distinctly by expressing its edges and joints. A decorative casing frames the door opening and sets it apart from the wall. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order (Articulation of Form).

q: Negative space in design is also called what?
n: Negative space, also called white space, is the empty space around and between objects. It is as active in a composition as the objects themselves. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order (Form and Space); Lupton, Graphic Design: The New Basics.

q: Who designed a memorial composed of below-grade black granite walls in a V shape, 247 feet long, whose granite panels carry the names of more than 58,000 soldiers who died in the Vietnam War?
n: Maya Lin designed the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, DC (1982). She won the national competition as a Yale undergraduate. Its black granite walls form a V and list over 58,000 names. Source: National Park Service, Vietnam Veterans Memorial.

q: The 2022 Pritzker Prize laureate is notable for what kind of projects?
n: Diébédo Francis Kéré, the 2022 Pritzker laureate from Burkina Faso, is recognized for community architecture, such as schools and clinics built with and for local communities using local materials. Source: The Pritzker Architecture Prize, 2022 Laureate announcement.

q: Who designed the US Capitol which is the seat of the United States Congress?
n: Dr. William Thornton won the 1793 design competition for the United States Capitol. Later architects completed it, including Latrobe, Bulfinch and Walter. Source: Architect of the Capitol, History of the U.S. Capitol.

q: Who designed the Jefferson Memorial in Washington, DC?
n: John Russell Pope designed the Jefferson Memorial (completed 1943), a Neoclassical rotunda modeled on the Pantheon. Source: National Park Service, Thomas Jefferson Memorial.

q: The Aga Khan Award for Architecture (AKAA) is a famous architectural prize awarding architectural projects successfully addressing the needs and aspirations of
n: The Aga Khan Award for Architecture, founded by Aga Khan IV in 1977, rewards projects that address the needs and aspirations of Muslim (Islamic) societies. Source: Aga Khan Development Network, Aga Khan Award for Architecture.

q: What is usually the minimum horizontal distance between fire sprinkler heads?
n: NFPA 13 requires sprinklers to be at least 1.8 m (6 ft) apart. Closer heads can wet adjacent ones ("cold soldering") and delay their activation. Source: NFPA 13, Sec. 10.2.5.3 (minimum distance between sprinklers); RA 9514 RIRR (adopts NFPA 13).

q: What is the usual class of mortar used for plastering?
n: Plaster mortar is commonly a Class B mix, 1 part cement to 3 parts sand. Class A (1:2) is used for richer, stronger mortar. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Mortar and Plaster Proportions).

q: One tin of paint is equal to how many gallons?
n: A tin (pail) of paint holds 4 gallons. A gallon is about 4 liters, and a quart is a quarter gallon. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Painting); local paint packaging conventions.

q: Onduline is a famous trademarked brand of what material?
n: Onduline is the trade name of lightweight corrugated roofing sheets made of bitumen-saturated organic fibers. Source: Onduline product literature; Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction (bituminous roofing).
